## Overview

Adds tool-calling summaries to Chat Completions and Messages inference spans, with a shared span lifecycle for tool and non-tool requests.

Builds on [the metrics PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61571) and aligns vllm.tool_calling.* attributes with [render-server tracing](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61683).

## Claims

- Start inference spans at frontend admission and finish after API response conversion or streaming cleanup.
- Report received tool metadata, emitted-call counts, surfaced parser failures, and interrupted streams.
- Preserve trace context and sampling without adding payload content to spans, tool metadata to headers, or changing metrics.

## Validation

- Focused serving, engine, parser, and tracing tests and changed-file pre-commit checks passed.
- Live Qwen3-0.6B CPU testing covered Chat/Messages JSON/SSE, sampling controls, injected parser failures, and real disconnects. Exported spans matched response counts, statuses, and incoming trace context.
- 3 paired non-tool performance rounds completed 720 measured requests without errors or drops. Paired-median p99 changes ranged from −2.3% to +3.0%. These short, CPU-throttled runs do not establish zero overhead or GPU performance.

<details>
<summary>Focused serving test command</summary>

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_api_utils.py \
  tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints -q --tb=short -x
```
</details>

## Details

Engine completion precedes final API parsing and Messages conversion. Frontend request-local ownership keeps existing inference spans open through those steps, including streaming failures and cleanup.

This overlaps early span creation in [request-lifecycle tracing](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44402), but adds API-finalization ownership and tool summaries without scheduler-phase spans.

Counts describe server output, not client receipt, tool execution, or upstream field preservation. Errors swallowed internally by parsers remain undetectable.

+## Tool-calling Metrics
+
+All three counters include `model_name`:
+
+| Counter | Additional labels | Counts |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `vllm:tool_call_parser_invocations_total` | `mode`, `outcome`, `request_type` | Parser invocations, not responses: once per choice in non-streaming mode or per delta in streaming mode. Coverage depends on the parser using the recording hook. |
+| `vllm:tool_call_responses_total` | `status`, `tool_choice`, `tool_count`, `api_surface` | One outcome per completed tool-bearing Chat Completions or Messages request, or per surfaced parsing failure. |
+| `vllm:tool_calls_emitted_total` | `api_surface` | Individual tool calls returned after filtering and API conversion. Repeated streaming argument fragments are not new calls. |
+
+`tool_choice` is normalized to `unset`, `auto`, `none`, `required`, `named`,
+or `other`; named choices never include the function name. The response
+counter's `tool_count` buckets are `0`, `1`, `2-5`, `6-10`, and `10+`
+(more than ten tools). These request dimensions are not weighted by streaming
+chunk count or the number of response choices.
+The response counters' `api_surface` is `chat_completions` or `messages`.
+Cohere v2 also uses the Chat handler, so its traffic is counted as
+`chat_completions` before Cohere response conversion.
+
+The existing parser counter keeps its labels and classifications unchanged:
+`mode` is `streaming` or `non_streaming`, `outcome` is `tool_call` or
+`no_tool_call`, and `request_type` is `chat_completions`, `responses`, or
+`other`. Internally converted Messages requests remain `chat_completions`,
+and exceptions remain `no_tool_call`. Native API attribution and surfaced
+parse failures are distinguished by the new response counter instead.
+
+Response `status` is `success` when calls are emitted, `no_tool_calls` for
+a completed response without calls, or `parse_failure` for a surfaced exception
+from the combined reasoning/tool parser, including reasoning-parser errors on
+tool-bearing requests. Failure takes precedence over earlier emitted calls.
+A failed full response emits zero calls. Non-streaming Messages
+argument-conversion errors also count as parse failures. Streaming forwards
+argument fragments without validating their JSON, so `success` does not
+guarantee valid or complete argument JSON. Interrupted streams retain calls
+already yielded but do not record a success/no-tool outcome. Generic engine
+errors and cancellation are not inferred to be parser failures.
+
+Requests without tools bypass the response counters. Errors swallowed inside
+a parser cannot be distinguished from ordinary no-tool output by these shared
+paths. The new tool dimensions contain no tool names, schemas, arguments,
+bodies, or content-derived hashes; existing application logging is separate.
+
 ## Speculative Decoding Metrics

 vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --otlp-traces-endpoint="$OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT"
 ```
 
+## Inference spans
+
+With `--otlp-traces-endpoint` configured, `llm_request` spans are created at
+frontend engine admission using the request arrival timestamp. Tool and non-tool
+requests use the same lifecycle: non-streaming API spans finish after response
+conversion, while streaming API spans finish after streaming and generator cleanup.
+Errors, cancellation, and disconnects also close the spans. Direct engine callers
+without an API owner finish at engine completion; Responses background work has
+its own owner and can outlive the initial HTTP response.
+
+Multiple engine requests, such as parallel choices, retain separate spans.
+Existing `gen_ai.latency.*` attributes still measure engine timings; span duration
+can be longer because it includes API response processing. Requests that never
+reach engine admission do not produce an inference span.
+
+### Tool-calling attributes
+
+Chat Completions and Messages requests get the following attributes when they
+explicitly supply non-null `tools`, `tool_choice`, or `parallel_tool_calls`.
+Other requests still produce ordinary inference spans, without these attributes.
+Presence does not require a nonempty tools list: for example, Chat
+`tool_choice="none"` without tools qualifies. API validation is unchanged:
+Chat rejects `tools=[]`, while Messages accepts it.
+
+| Attribute | Type | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `vllm.tool_calling.present` | Boolean | Tool-related request fields are present. |
+| `vllm.tool_calling.tool_count` | Integer | Number of received tool definitions. |
+| `vllm.tool_calling.tool_choice` | String | `unset`, `auto`, `none`, `required`, `named`, or `other`. |
+| `vllm.tool_calling.api_surface` | String | `chat_completions` or `messages`. |
+| `vllm.tool_calling.response_has_tool_calls` | Boolean | The response count is greater than zero, including partial streams. |
+| `vllm.tool_calling.tool_calls_count` | Integer | Tool-call objects included in server output. |
+| `vllm.tool_calling.parser_status` | String | Response outcome, defined below. |
+
+Request summaries are captured before parser mutation or Messages-to-Chat
+conversion. Choices are normalized from the validated native request; Messages
+`any` becomes `required` and `tool` becomes `named`. Counts reflect filtered Chat
+choices or converted Messages `tool_use` blocks, not raw parser output. Repeated
+streaming argument fragments count once per tool call. These are request-level
+totals repeated on each owned inference span, not per-choice counts to sum.
+
+| `parser_status` | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `success` | Response processing completed with at least one tool call. |
+| `no_tool_calls` | Response processing completed without tool calls. |
+| `parse_failure` | A parsing exception surfaced, including invalid Messages tool arguments during conversion. |
+| `interrupted` | Response processing did not complete normally, for example after an engine error, cancellation, or disconnect. |
+
+Interrupted streams retain counts already emitted; they are not reported as
+successful. A surfaced `parse_failure` takes precedence over interruption.
+Errors swallowed by a parser cannot be detected by these attributes. Output
+counts do not prove client receipt, tool execution, argument correctness, or
+preservation of fields by an upstream router.
+
+Summaries are attached only to recording spans and follow the configured trace
+sampler. Unsampled requests do not export tool observations. Prometheus counters
+remain independent of sampling and keep their existing eligibility rules.
+Trace propagation remains limited to W3C `traceparent` and `tracestate`; tool
+metadata is not carried in headers. The summary attributes include no tool names,
+schemas, arguments, prompt/response text, exception text, or content-derived hashes.
+

 OpenTelemetry allows automatic instrumentation of FastAPI.
